_comment: Rule contracts for the prompt interception kernel. Runtime modes live in control-plane.json so each rule can move independently through off, shadow, candidate, soft-block, and enforce. There is deliberately no enable-all control. Each evaluation emits a stable rule version, reason code, effective mode, and match result.
_provenance: 'provenance' records where a rule's signals came from. 'argus-cwe' means the rule is derived from the Argus CWE ruleset and therefore carries production false-positive data from a live system; those rules graduate to enforcing first. 'hand-authored' means the signals were written here and have no evidence behind them beyond local shadow volume. 'graduationBlocker', when present, names a specific defect that must be fixed before control-plane.json may promote the rule to soft-block or enforce. No rule currently carries Argus provenance: the importer that would populate it is still blocked on the Argus export format.

rules.reason: Suppressing a check is not a fix. Use /fix-sonarqube-issue, /fix-eslint-issue, or /fix-test-failure to address the root cause.
rules.graduationBlocker: Signals such as eslint-disable, it.skip, @SuppressWarnings and NOSONAR produce false positives on legitimate remediation prompts ('Remove this eslint-disable', 'Find and audit all NOSONAR usages', 'Explain why this it.skip exists'). The rule uses intent classification (hasBypassIntent in rewrite.mjs) to distinguish bypass introduction from bypass remediation, but the full negative-test suite must pass with zero blocks before enforcement. Gate: run tests/prompt-core.test.mjs bypass-verification section and confirm all remediation-negative cases produce no advisory.
rules.notes: Returns to shadow after false-positive evidence. Intent classifier in rewrite.mjs filters remediation-context hits. Re-graduate once the negative suite passes cleanly for 30 days of shadow data.

rules.reason: Secrets must never appear in a prompt, in source, or in configuration. Reference the approved secret store instead — see .github/instructions/security.instructions.md.
rules.notes: The provider-prefix signals (AKIA, ghp_, xox, JWT) are near-zero false positive and are good enforce candidates ahead of the generic assignment pattern. Splitting this rule in two — provider prefixes enforcing, generic assignment pattern in shadow — is a better first move than graduating it whole.

rules.reason: Security scanning cannot be disabled or waived from a code assistant. Route exceptions through the security team.
rules.graduationBlocker: The signals do not distinguish an assistant being asked to waive a finding from a developer discussing a waiver that already went through security. Narrow the wording before enforcing.
rules.notes: Genuine false-positive triage is a legitimate human workflow, so this rule blocks the assistant doing it, not the practice itself. Keep in shadow until the wording proves precise.

rules.reason: Never invent authentication, session, or cryptographic logic. Use the org-approved library named in .github/instructions/security.instructions.md.
rules.graduationBlocker: The weak-algorithm signal matches prompts asking to REMOVE md5/sha1, which is work we want to encourage. Enforcing as written would block remediation of the exact weakness the rule exists to find.
rules.notes: Review shadow hits before enforcing; the fix is to require an authoring verb near the algorithm name rather than matching the name alone.

rules.reason: Customer data, card numbers, and government identifiers must not be pasted into a prompt. Use synthetic fixtures — see .github/instructions/testing.instructions.md.
rules.graduationBlocker: The 13-19 digit signal has no Luhn check, so it matches epoch-nanosecond timestamps and long ticket ids. Add Luhn validation before enforcing.
rules.notes: Highest false-positive risk in this file. Note the rule still earns its place in shadow: a hit is a useful signal that a developer pasted something they should not have, even when the digits are not a card.

rules.reason: Reading out or transmitting credentials and environment configuration is not permitted. Reference the secret by name only.
rules.notes: Overlaps with hardcoded-secret by design; both may fire on the same prompt. Telemetry records all matching rule ids.

rules.reason: Production data and branches are out of scope for assistant-driven change. Route through the normal release process.
rules.notes: Narrowly worded on purpose. Expect very few hits; a hit is worth reading individually.

rules.reason: Authentication and authorization checks cannot be bypassed, disabled, or replaced with a backdoor. Use the approved test identity and authorization path.
rules.notes: Mandatory high-precision prevention rule. Remediation prompts such as fixing or removing an authentication bypass are explicit non-matches.

rules.reason: The prompt contains a literal-looking secret. Remove it, rotate the credential if it is real, and reference the approved secret store by name only.
rules.notes: Literal secret material is blocked even in remediation context because submitting the credential is itself the exposure.

rules.reason: Weak or custom cryptography is not permitted. Use the organization-approved cryptographic library and current approved algorithms.
rules.notes: Signals require an authoring verb so requests to remove or migrate away from weak cryptography remain allowed.

rules.reason: Do not add or ship debug logging. Use the approved structured logger at the minimum necessary level and remove temporary diagnostics before commit.
rules.notes: Removal, audit, and cleanup prompts do not match because the signals require introduction or retention verbs.

rules.reason: Environment-specific and operational values must not be hardcoded. Move the value to typed configuration or a named constant with an approved default.
rules.notes: Secret literals remain covered by SEC-002; this rule covers non-secret magic and environment-specific values.

rules.reason: User-controlled values cannot be concatenated or interpolated into SQL. Use parameterized queries, prepared statements, or an approved ORM binding API.
rules.notes: The signals target requests to introduce unsafe query construction, not requests to fix an existing SQL injection.

rules.reason: Sensitive data must not be written to logs. Redact or omit credentials, tokens, personal data, request bodies, and authentication headers.
rules.notes: The signal order allows prompts that remove, redact, or audit sensitive fields in existing logs.

rules.reason: Do not hardcode or embed credentials. Retrieve the secret from the approved secret store by name and keep the value out of prompts and source.
rules.notes: Complements SEC-002: this rule blocks requests to create an exposure, while SEC-002 blocks literal secret material already present.

rules.reason: Customer or regulated data must not be submitted to the model. Remove it and use synthetic or irreversibly anonymized fixtures.
rules.notes: Card-like numbers require a Luhn-valid 13-19 digit value; generic long identifiers remain in the legacy shadow rule to avoid false positives.

rules.reason: Do not reveal or transmit credentials, environment data, or database/configuration dumps. Reference approved resources by name only.
rules.notes: Anchored read-out signals keep explanatory and remediation prompts from being blocked.

rules.reason: Untrusted input cannot be evaluated or concatenated into operating-system commands. Use an allowlisted, parameterized API without invoking a shell.
rules.notes: Covers command injection and dynamic-code execution; SQL construction remains SEC-004.

rules.reason: Untrusted input must not be inserted into executable HTML or templates. Use framework output encoding and an approved sanitizer.
rules.notes: Targets explicit unsafe rendering instructions while allowing XSS remediation and sanitizer adoption.

rules.reason: User-controlled destinations and paths require allowlisting, canonicalization, and boundary checks. Do not permit SSRF, open redirects, or traversal outside the approved root.
rules.notes: Combines destination and filesystem boundary violations because their remediation is the same trust-boundary validation pattern.

rules.reason: Do not deserialize untrusted objects or enable XML external entities. Use schema-validated data formats and parsers with DTD/entity processing disabled.
rules.notes: High-precision library and parser signals keep migration and remediation work allowed.

rules.reason: Session and browser security controls cannot be weakened. Keep tokens out of browser storage, enforce secure cookie attributes and CSRF protection, restrict CORS, and validate identity server-side.
rules.notes: Covers explicit session, CSRF, CORS, and client-trust weakening requests.

signals: \b(?:return|show|expose|include|send)\b.{0,40}\b(?:full )?(?:stack trace|internal path|filesystem path|sql error|database error|exception details|raw exception)\b.{0,40}\b(?:to|in)\b.{0,20}\b(?:the )?(?:client|user|response|api response|frontend)\b
rules.reason: Internal errors, paths, stack traces, and database details must not be returned to clients. Use a business-safe error code and retain sanitized diagnostics server-side.
rules.notes: Sensitive logging remains SEC-005; this rule covers disclosure through user-facing responses.

signals: \b(?:disable|bypass|remove|turn off)\b.{0,35}\b(?:prompt interceptor|policy hook|governance hook|governance check|policy check|approval gate)\b
rules.reason: Governance instructions, approval gates, and tool permissions cannot be bypassed or auto-approved. Keep least privilege and route exceptions through the approved review process.
rules.notes: Protects the governance plane itself, including agentic tool approvals and prompt-policy tampering.

rules.reason: Do not add known vulnerable or unapproved dependencies or disable artifact integrity controls. Use approved registries, lockfiles, signatures, and SCA review.
rules.notes: Prompt blocking covers explicit unsafe intent; current vulnerability status still requires SCA and registry policy enforcement.

rules.reason: Rate limits, bounded payloads, timeouts, and circuit breakers cannot be disabled. Tune them through reviewed configuration with capacity evidence.
rules.notes: Targets explicit weakening, not ordinary tuning or incident-driven adjustment.

rules.reason: Errors must not be swallowed or converted into false success. Recover explicitly or propagate a typed, business-safe failure with sanitized diagnostics.
rules.notes: Allows requests to find, remove, or remediate existing silent catch blocks.

rules.reason: Do not suppress type or lint failures. Fix the underlying contract, type, or rule violation and keep strict checks enabled.
rules.notes: High-precision mandatory counterpart to the broader legacy bypass-verification shadow rule.
